kf: **Irritant blistering** from **cantharidin** in blister beetles: the beetle doesn't bite; lesions follow crushing it on skin.
**Paederus (rove beetle) dermatitis** is the look-alike: toxin paederin, **linear and "kissing" lesions**.
Blisters appear within about a day, often on exposed skin after night-time exposure near lights.
First aid: blow or flick beetles off, **don't crush**; wash with soap and water.
Treat with cool compresses and a short potent topical steroid (milder on face); antibiotics only if infected.
myths: **"It's shingles"**: linear lesions without dermatomal pain and with a beetle history point to Paederus.
patho_lead: Beetle toxins **break the bonds between skin cells**, so the epidermis splits.

mech.t: Crushing the beetle releases cantharidin (or paederin) onto skin.
A superficial blister forms with little dermal inflammation, so it heals without scarring.
Toxin transfers to opposing skin folds (elbow crease, neck).

comp: Secondary infection, eye involvement (Nairobi eye), post-inflammatory pigmentation.
